This appeal has been filed by the appellant/Insurance company under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act arising out of award dated 29.10.2018 passed by 8th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur District-Jabalpur in Claim Case No. 51/2016 seeking exoneration from liability to pay the compensation.

Therefore, Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation.

It is also urged that FIR (Ex.P/2) has been lodged on the next day of incident and it has been lodged by father of deceased and in FIR, it is mentioned that deceased was sitting on the tractor when tractor turned turtle.

It is also urged that in final report (Ex.P/1), it has NEUTRAL CITATION NO.

Further, after referring to para-9 of PW-1, wife of deceased, it is urged that therein witness has admitted that at the time of accident, her husband was sitting on tractor.
It is also urged that statement of witnesses (Ex.P/10 to P/14) has been recorded on 10.12.2015 i.e. after a delay of almost 15 days because incident occurred on 27.11.2015.
Further, after relying on Oriental Insurance Company Limited Vs. Premlata Shukla and Others (2007) 13 SCC 476,

3. Learned counsel for the respondents No.1 to 3/claimants, after referring to para-17, 18 and 19 of impugned award as well as statements of applicant witnesses- 2 and 3 and (Ex.P/10 to P/14),
submits that from aforesaid, it is clearly established that at the time of accident, deceased was not sitting in the tractor and he was going on his foot and he has been hit from behind by the offending tractor.
It is also urged that FIR is not substantive piece of evidence.
On above grounds, it is urged that findings recorded by the Tribunal in para-17, 18 and 19 are well supported by the evidence on record.
No interference is required in the same.

With respect to above submissions, learned counsel for the respondents has relied upon National Insurance Company Ltd Vs. Dilip Kumar Jain and Others (2019) NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:541 3 MA-711-2019 AAC 1058 a n d Halappa Vs. Malik Sab (2018) 1 ACC 163.

sentences.text: On above grounds, it is urged that appeal filed by the Insurance Company be dismissed.
4 . I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused record of the case.

5. Perusal of submissions of learned counsel for the parties reveals that the sole issue involved in the case is whether at the time of accident, deceased was travelling on the tractor/sitting on the tractor or he was going on foot and he was hit by the offending tractor.

With respect to above, this Court has examined the documents available on record, especially, filed by the respondents/claimants,
deposition of applicant witnesses and findings recorded by Tribunal in impugned award.
6.

So far as documentary evidence with respect to issue involved in the case is concerned, perusal of FIR (Ex.P/2) reveals that it has been lodged on 28.11.2015 with respect to accident that occurred on 27.11.2015.
Aforesaid FIR has been lodged by father of the deceased.
In FIR (Ex.P/2), it is clearly mentioned that on 27.11.2015, ........ his son Santosh was sitting on tractor which was being driven by owner of tractor Sammat Singh and he was going to the field.
It is also mentioned in the FIR that driver of tractor was driving tractor rashly and negligently and he overturned tractor on the culvert.
On account of which, his son Santosh came under the tractor.
Thus, from above FIR, it is evident that at the time of accident, deceased was sitting/was travelling on the tractor.

It is nowhere mentioned in the FIR that at the time of accident, deceased was going on foot and he was hit by the offending NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:541 4 MA-711-2019 tractor driven by Sammat Singh.
7. It is also evident from record of the case that father of deceased is also one of the applicants, who have filed claim petition for compensation.
But respondents/claimants have not examined father of deceased, who lodged aforesaid FIR and no explanation has been furnished for not examining him.
8. It is correct that FIR in itself is not a substantive piece of evidence.

But in the instant case,
aforesaid FIR (Ex.P/2) has been filed by the claimants itself in the case.

Hon'ble Apex Court in Premlata Shukla (Supra) has clearly held that where parts of a documents have been relied on by both the parties, then, the same may be relied on irrespective of whether the contents of document United India Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Smt. Saivati Bai Ureti on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123631848/
2 have been proved or not.

sentences.text: In the instant case, FIR (Ex.P/2) has been filed by the claimants themselves.

Therefore, they cannot argue and take defence that contents of the FIR are not correct,
especially when, they have not examined father of deceased, who lodged the FIR and have not furnished any explanation for not examining him.

9 . Hence, in view of law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in Premlata Shukla (Supra) and Division Bench of this Court in Arun Kumar Patel (Supra), respondents/claimants cannot say that the contents of FIR are not correct.

1 0 . Further, applicant's witness Smt. Saivati Bai (AW-1), wife of deceased, has admitted in para-9 of her cross-examination that it is correct that her husband had gone on the tractor itself which overturned at the scene of accident.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:541 5 MA-711-2019 11.
Again, other applicant witnesses Kishan Lal and Lallu Singh has deposed that at the time of accident, deceased was taking tractor and he was going ahead of the tractor.
No applicant witness has deposed that at the time of accident, deceased was going on bicycle/motorcycle etc.
Further, no such vehicle has been recovered from the scene of incident.
Thus, if testimony of applicant witness Kishanlal and Lallu Singh is treated as/taken as true, then, at the time of accident, deceased was going on foot.
Then, in above scenario, it is highly unnatural and improbable that a person going on foot would be going at the speed of a tractor.

Thus, if deposition of applicant witnesses, especially,
Kishanlal and Lallu Singh, is tested on the anvil of probability, then also, their depositions do not inspire confidence and hence, they are not reliable.

12. Hence, in view of discussion in the foregoing paras, in view of factual difference, principles laid down in Dilip Kumar Jain (Supra) and Malik Sab (Supra) do not help respondents/claimants in any way.
There is nothing on record to show that at the time of accident, deceased was trying to get on the tractor etc.

Therefore, just on the basis of charge-sheet, it cannot be said that at the time of accident, deceased was not sitting on the tractor/was not travelling on the tractor.
13.

Hence, in view of discussion in the foregoing paras, in this Court's considered opinion, findings recorded by the Tribunal to the effect that at the time of accident, deceased was travelling on foot are not correct and they are contrary to evidence on record.
14.

Resultantly, findings recorded by the Tribunal with respect to NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:541 6 MA-711-2019 above in para-13 to 19, so far as they relate to deceased not sitting or travelling on tractor at the time of accident, are set aside.

15. Hence, in this Court's opinion, from evidence on record, it is clearly established that at the time of accident, deceased was sitting on the tractor/was traveling on the tractor when it overturned.

Hence, Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation {National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Rattani and Others (Supra)}.

sentences.text: Resultantly, in view of discussion in the foregoing paras, appeal filed by the appellant-Insurance Company is allowed and Insurance Company is exonerated from liability to pay the compensation and it is held that only owner and driver of offending vehicle (respondents Phool Singh and Sammat Singh) are liable to pay the compensation as adjudged by the Tribunal in the impugned award.
Other terms and conditions of award shall remain intact.
Impugned award passed by the Tribunal is modified to the extent as aforesaid.
1 7 . Appeal filed by appellant-Insurance Company is allowed and disposed of accordingly.
